title: local-workflow ship survives a disk-full gate: refuse a doomed gate up front, reclaim idle caches and rerun once, name the cause
goal: A whole-workspace gate that ran out of disk failed after ten minutes of compiling with rustc's 'IO failure on output stream' and 'failed to parse process output', and the ship reported a generic gate failure. Before the gates start, measure the free space of the candidate's filesystem and refuse a gate below a measured floor (12 GiB for a whole-workspace gate on a cold target, 4 GiB warm, 2 GiB narrowed) after reclaiming the ship's own idle caches: warm targets stashed for idle slots, those slots' leftover candidate targets and the legacy integration target, never a busy slot's or this candidate's. When a gate still fails with a disk-full signature, reclaim and run that gate once more, keep the first log beside the rerun's, and record the reclaim in the evidence; a failure that remains names the free space instead of reading like a compiler bug. The same applies to the commercial gate.
